title: Healey’s Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds
summary:
There have been almost no Budget leaks.
The chancellor's aides are using intelligence-style security measures to guard its secrets: the Budget has been split into "compartments" with very few given access to all of them.
The IT has been locked down and ministers viewing the plans have to sign a digital promise not to brief media.
Such security is a response to the feeling that speculation around the last Budget, sometimes informed by insiders, was economically destabilising.
The economic news has been good - growth has been better than expected and the International Monetary Fund has endorsed the UK for "standing out" among the G7 countries for at least planning to cut borrowing.

title: Inflation under Trump is only about half the rate under Biden. Voters are still just as mad.
summary:
So far in President Trump's second term, prices in the US have risen only about half as quickly as during his predecessor's four years in office.
Yet Trump has a 72% disapproval rating on the issue and risks paying a steep political price — just as former President Biden did — with voters drawing a direct connection between rising prices and the president's policies.
During the last election cycle, prices of all items rose more than 20% in Biden's term , sparking widespread voter angst.
Trump has often pushed back against questions about high energy prices, saying they won't be a problem once the war in Iran ends.
Toys are a particularly stark example, falling by 4.6% during Biden's term and then rising by 7.8% so far in Trump's term.

title: Americans have never had more of their money in stocks — not even in the dot-com bubble: Chart of the Day
summary:
Stocks made up 48.2% of Americans' financial assets in the second quarter, counting everything from brokerage accounts to 401(k)s, according to the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Accounts data.
It tops the 38.7% reached at the height of the dot-com mania and the 41% hit after the 2021 meme-stock frenzy.
Households hold about $74 trillion in stocks against roughly $20 trillion in bank deposits and money market funds — a record $3.65 in stocks for every dollar of cash.
When stocks rally and everything else sits still, stocks take up a bigger slice of the pie on their own.
A low share means plenty of money is left to move into stocks, usually at bargain prices.

title: Forget the House and the Senate, the economy may hinge on state and local races in the midterm elections
summary:
Data centers have emerged as a national issue during this midterm election cycle, and candidates for the House and Senate have seized on it in their campaigns.
But state and local officials actually have more sway over data center construction and energy infrastructure, so the winners of lower-profile races may hold the economy's future in their hands.
That dynamic was on display on Tuesday, when Amazon canceled a plan to build data centers in Loudoun County, Virginia, after reaching an agreement with local officials amid widespread backlash from residents.
Greg Abbott has turned from a data center booster to a skeptic as he faces a tough re-election race against Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa.
Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, also observed that midterm races for state capitals and town halls represent a bigger risk to the data center buildout than what happens in Washington, D.C.

title: Bangladesh per capita GDP forecast to outstrip India’s: What does it mean?
summary:
Bangladesh is expected to surpass India’s per capita GDP this year, but the complete economic picture is a mix of success stories and new challenges.
Share Bangladesh per capita GDP forecast to outstrip India’s: What does it mean?
But its neighbour’s per capita GDP, which is GDP divided by the total population, is expected to surpass that of India, the world’s most populous nation.
In 2029, based on current growth forecasts, India’s per capita GDP of $3,661 would top Bangladesh’s $3,334, according to the IMF.
Experts noted that Bangladesh is facing a weaker near-term growth outlook, even as its projected GDP per capita edges above India’s.
